title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks with price at $10.81 saw sales 49 and 31 units (vs baseline 34.8). The lower sales suggest a negative price effect. Noise-adjusted price sensitivity is supported by this consistent pattern.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no events and a 5.5% price increase to $10.81. Recent weeks show no trend or seasonal ramp beyond the baseline. The price increase is above regular ($10.25), and past price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 49 and 31 units respectively—below baseline (34.8). The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is negative, with no past promotion at this price point. The uplift model suggests no effect, and evidence for price sensitivity is stronger than for any event. No drivers justify a multiplier above 1.0. The baseline uncertainty is already well-calibrated.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.8 | 5%-95%: 18.2 - 58.5 | 10%-90%: 20.6 - 55.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
